# Canon Clerk

> Canon Clerk is an open specification and emerging semantic linter for software architecture, engineering conventions, and project tenets.

Canon Clerk addresses the asymmetric cognitive tax placed on maintainers by AI code generators: generative coding tools accelerate code production, generating pull requests that pass static tests and AST linters, but quietly violate unwritten architectural tenets and project conventions. Canon Clerk formalizes these rules into zero-friction Markdown files stored in `.canons/` and audits changes using an efficient three-stage evaluation cascade.

Key architectural concepts:
- **Dual Pillars:** The project encompasses both the **Canon Standard** (an open specification for declarative, natural-language architectural invariants) and the **Clerk Runner** (the CI review gate and CLI engine that executes multi-stage LLM evaluation).
- **Core Platform:** Canon Clerk is an automated review engine and specification platform, not a shell utility or script collection; helper scripts in `.agents/skills/` are auxiliary automation tools for AI coding assistants.
- **Evaluation Cascade:** Audits execute across three stages—Stage 0 Deterministic Path Filter (0 tokens), Stage 1 Fast Screener (lightweight model), and Stage 2 Deep Auditor (frontier reasoning model).

## The Canon Standard

- [The Canon Corpus](README.md#the-canon-corpus): Index and overview of modular, domain-scoped canons governing CLI ergonomics, canon authoring, visual identity, AI skills, and commit standards.
- [Canon Format Specification](SPEC.md): Complete normative grammar, What/When/Why/How tetrad, metadata derivation rules (id, title, triggers, inspect, tags, references), directive contracts (Exception, Remediation, Rationale), and progressive disclosure tiers.
- [Canon Authoring Canons](.canons/canon-authoring/): Reusable, project-agnostic exemplars tagged `canon-authoring` codifying canon-authoring invariants (naming, atomicity, falsifiability, semantic scope, succinctness, and directive contracts).
- [README Authoring Canons](.canons/readme-authoring/): Reusable, project-agnostic exemplars tagged `readme-authoring` codifying landing documentation invariants (orientation, feature parity, roadmap omission, responsive hero banners, and architecture shunting).
- [Visual Identity Canons](.canons/visual-identity/): Reusable exemplars tagged `visual-identity` codifying brand iconography isolation and alpha transparency.
- [OpenSpec Canons](.canons/openspec/): Reusable exemplars tagged `openspec` codifying Spec-Driven Development invariants for features and bug fixes.
- [Dogfood Canons](.canons/internal/): Internal project governance policies tagged `internal` enforced in CI on this repository.

## The Clerk Runner

- [Architecture & Evaluation Cascade](docs/architecture.md): Architectural specification of the three-stage evaluation cascade (Stage 0 Path Filter, Stage 1 Fast Screener, Stage 2 Deep Auditor) and the four-verdict matrix.
- [Target Audience & Problem Space](README.md#who-needs-this): Friction points, target personas, and engineering use cases for semantic linting.
- [Workspace Packages](packages/): TypeScript monorepo packages comprising schema definitions, core evaluation engine, CLI tooling, and GitHub Action runner.
- [Living Specifications](openspec/specs/): Formal architectural specifications and interface contracts for the evaluation engine, CLI, and GitHub Action.

## Agent & Contributor Orientation

- [Agent Guidelines](AGENTS.md): Operational orientation, architectural anchors, and workspace navigation instructions for AI coding assistants.
- [Development Workflow](docs/development-workflow.md): Complete development guide covering issue claiming, triangular Git worktrees, Conventional Commit matrices, and pull request lifecycles.
- [Conventional Commit Reference](docs/conventional-commits.md): Normative Conventional Commit matrix, surface-to-prefix mapping, SemVer rules, and GitHub label taxonomy.

## Optional

- [Development Setup](docs/development-setup.md): Guide to local machine onboarding, bare Git clone setup, triangular worktrees, Node.js toolchain, and GitHub CLI configuration.
- [Contributing Guide](docs/contributing.md): Contribution policies, Google Contributor License Agreement (CLA), and squash-merge expectations.
- [Project Readme](README.md): Human-oriented project homepage, architectural problem statement, progressive disclosure tiers, and overview.
